name: Test Race
crewNotes:
Warm salty liquids are what work late — cup-o-noodles, broth, quesadillas. Dry food gets hard to swallow. Proven foods: PB&J, Uncrustables, Oreos, Nutter Butters, watermelon, pretzels.

If I'm struggling — tight stomach, hoarse voice, heart rate climbing, not eating — it's almost always SODIUM AND FLUID, not calories. Push an LMNT, not a gel. This is my known failure mode.

When it's hot: refill my ice bandana and pour two cups of cold water over my head. Makes a massive difference. Offer it in case I forget to ask.

Salt pills come in counted containers with the number in sharpie. Pills left = pills not taken. Check them at every stop and tell me the number.

Expect two or more bathroom stops over the race. Normal for me. Not a problem. If I go and it's not solid, give me Imodium.

When I go quiet, ask me direct questions with numbers: how many gels this leg, when did you last pee, what sounds good right now. Don't ask "how are you feeling."

I can nap 15–20 minutes and come back fine. Offer it if I'm fading.

Music only when I'm struggling - it's a tool, not background.

I DNF'd here at mile 86 in 2025. The second night is the fight.
